faf4480c2e9fa0217e8eb9413078470a84ac0924.summary: The Register article (4 June 2012) reports on Tinba, a 20KB banking Trojan also known as Zusy. It hooks into browsers, uses Man in the Browser tricks to alter banking sites and get around two-factor authentication, and steals login data. Its command-and-control traffic is RC4-encrypted and goes to four hardcoded domains. Researchers at CSIS Security say antivirus detection of the analysed samples is low. The article compares Tinba with ZeuS and the Flame toolkit. Most of the page is unrelated news.
